Break it down.
Build it up.

I'm Diyelo Dulay. Since 2019 I've worked as a failure analysis technician at Advanced Energy, where my job is to find out why things fail. I started in electromechanics at Dualtech, and I learned most of the rest hands-on at the bench. Breaking a problem down taught me how things work, so now I want to build them: power supplies, solar setups and the tools around them. This portfolio is where I practice that.

My story

I work as a Failure Analysis (FA) Technician at Advanced Energy in Laguna. My day is bench troubleshooting: tracing a failed unit down to the part, the process step or the test that caused it, then reporting it clearly to engineers and site leads.

My direction is power electronics together with electrical work: supplies, bridges, motor control, solar systems and the wiring and drawings that go with them. I am studying it by building small tools and diagrams I can check by hand.

I trained in Electromechanics Technology at Dualtech and I keep learning. Next, I plan to pursue a degree through CHED ETEEAP at Manuel S. Enverga University Foundation. I started coding to remove repeated paperwork, so every tool here is plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript that runs offline on a phone.

Education

Electromechanics Technology

Dualtech Training Center Foundation Inc. · Virtue and Work
  • A two-year, TESDA-registered program in Canlubang, Calamba, Laguna, at a technical school founded in 1982. Its tagline is “Virtue and Work”.
  • It follows the German Dual Training System, which the Philippines adopted in the Dual Training System Act of 1994 (RA 7686). There are two learning venues, the school and the industry, with about 30 % theory and 70 % hands-on practice.
  • Each student is assigned a tutor who coaches them one-on-one on life skills and on personal and professional development, so the school forms character as well as skills.
  • Electromechanics combines electrical, mechanical and electronics trades, and it is the base for the more advanced technical work I do now.
Entry 04 · On the bench

The bench

GENERIC EXAMPLE CASE · "unit does not power up". Tap a test point or a step. No company data is shown here.

Entry 04A · Power electronics

Power schematics

Pick a circuit, then step through its switching states. The orange line shows where the current flows. Ideal parts, teaching diagrams, not a design for production.

Motor control

Motor control

Hold a button to press it. The left diagram is the control circuit (ladder), the right one is the power circuit. Orange means current flows. Educational model, not a wiring plan for a real panel.

Wiring diagrams

Wiring diagrams

Press the switch buttons. Orange wire carries current. Teaching model: follow your local wiring code for real installations.

Technical drawing and shop

Drawing & shop

Practise reading a caliper and a micrometer, build a part in isometric and see its views, and check limits and fits.

Analog

Analog lab

Standard formulas for op-amp gain, filters, ADC resolution, thermistors and 4-20 ma loops. Ideal parts, so check the datasheet for your real ones.

Virtual lab

Sound room

Build a speaker system the way you build on the breadboard. Pick a layout or add speakers, drag them around the room, and read the angles, delays and cable runs. Turn sound on to hear it: tap a speaker, run the calibration noise, or play the demo. Use headphones for the 3D effect. A teaching model with simple panning, not a room-acoustics simulation.

Audio

Audio lab

Amp and speaker maths, class A, AB and D amplifiers, a split-rail linear supply, digital audio and crossovers. Ideal-part formulas, so real speakers and amps will differ.

Solar setup guide

Solar

On-grid, off-grid and hybrid: how the energy flows, how to size a system, how to check a panel string, and the order to install it. Learning notes, not a design. A licensed professional must sign off a real installation.

Experiment

Monitor

A diy monitoring system for any solar setup, branded or not. Sense the input and output of every device, see harvest, consumption and battery, and know when the line must back the system up. The dashboard runs on the system you built in solar / assemble. Simulated readings, with the hardware design for a real build. Mains and battery wiring must be done by a licensed electrician.

Virtual lab

Breadboard

Pick a part, tap two holes to place it, then read the result. Holes in the same column half are connected. The long rails run along the whole board. Three-leg parts take three taps. The meter is DC; the scope runs a time-domain simulation. Simplified teaching models.

          Professional summary

          Failure Analysis Technician with more than seven years of experience diagnosing component-level failures in AC-DC power supplies, DC-DC converters and PCBA assemblies. Skilled in root cause analysis, board-level repair and bench verification, and in passing technical knowledge across sites.

          Failure Analysis Technician · Advanced Energy Industries, LagunaJul 2019 – Present
          • Diagnose component-level failures in power supplies and converters through schematic analysis and bench measurements.
          • Perform root cause analysis, hard-failure investigations, recalibration, reprogramming and no-fault-found verification.
          • Carry out board-level troubleshooting and repair.
          • Write failure analysis reports and corrective-action recommendations for engineering, quality, process and production.
          • Built a work-in-progress tracking solution for units moving from production to failure analysis.
